title: Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment (Australian Grape and Wine Authority) Bill 2013
short_title: Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment (Australian Grape and Wine Authority) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update excise levy legislation to support the proposed Australian Grape and Wine Authority, allowing collected levies to be paid to that authority.
It would replace references and definitions linked to the Wine Australia Corporation and remove its special process for recommending levy rates after annual general meetings.
The levy amendments would take effect with the main merger bill’s provisions on 1 July 2014, without altering the structure or amounts of existing levies.
changes: The representative organisation definition for the grapes research levy would be aligned with the new authority’s legislation.
The old Corporation definition would be removed from the wine grapes levy schedule.
The declared winemakers’ organisation definition would refer to the new authority’s governing Act.
summary.affected: Grape growers and winemakers paying the relevant levies, their representative organisations and the Australian Grape and Wine Authority are affected.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Introduced a second companion bill updating the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act 1999 to replace references to the Wine Australia Corporation with the new Australian Grape and Wine Authority, and removed the requirement for Wine Australia's annual meeting to recommend levy rate changes, aligning the wine industry's levy process with other sectors.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Referred the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment (Australian Grape and Wine Authority) Bill 2013 and two related customs and excise levy bills to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill, noting Australia's wine exports to China grew from $57 million in 2007 to $250 million in 2013 but lag New Zealand due to the lack of a free trade agreement, and said the industry includes more than 2,500 wine producers and 6,000 grape growers.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill but warned that supermarket duopoly control of 60 to 70 per cent of retail wine sales was squeezing producers, citing a KPMG report showing trade spend paid to retailers rose from 19.5 to 23.4 per cent of gross sales between 2008-09 and 2011-12.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Concluded debate on the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill, confirming the merger followed an industry proposal submitted in August 2012 by Wine Grape Growers Australia and the Winemakers Federation of Australia, and said the coalition's review of the Competition and Consumer Act would examine unconscionable conduct provisions affecting small winemakers' ability to market their products.
